organisms.prevention: Hand hygiene; wound care; contact precautions for MRSA
organisms.learnMore: S. aureus is one of the most common causes of skin infections worldwide. About 30% of the population are asymptomatic nasal carriers. MRSA (methicillin-resistant S. aureus) is a major hospital and community pathogen.

organisms.learnMore: S. pneumoniae is the leading cause of community-acquired pneumonia and an important cause of meningitis. It has a polysaccharide capsule that is its major virulence factor and the basis for vaccine development.

organisms.learnMore: Tetanospasmin blocks inhibitory neurotransmitter release (GABA and glycine), causing uncontrolled muscle contractions. Despite effective vaccines, tetanus kills tens of thousands globally each year.

organisms.learnMore: Meningococcal disease can progress to death within 24 hours. The petechial rash from meningococcemia is due to DIC (disseminated intravascular coagulation).

organisms.learnMore: H. pylori colonizes over 50% of the world's population. It produces urease, which neutralizes stomach acid, allowing it to survive. It is a WHO Group 1 carcinogen.

organisms.learnMore: Pertussis toxin (PT) is an ADP-ribosyltransferase that disables Gi proteins, leading to uncontrolled adenylyl cyclase activity. Despite widespread vaccination, pertussis is resurgent due to waning immunity.

organisms.learnMore: Influenza A undergoes antigenic shift (reassortment of gene segments) and antigenic drift (point mutations). Shift causes pandemic strains; drift explains why annual vaccination is needed.

organisms.learnMore: SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds ACE2 receptors on host cells. The mRNA vaccines direct cells to produce spike protein, eliciting a protective immune response without using live virus.

organisms.name: Plasmodium falciparum

organisms.learnMore: P. falciparum causes ~90% of malaria deaths. Unlike other Plasmodium species, it can infect RBCs of all ages, causing extremely high parasitemia. Sequestration of infected RBCs in brain microvasculature causes cerebral malaria.

organisms.learnMore: T. gondii infects ~30% of the world's population. Most infections are asymptomatic in immunocompetent individuals, but the parasite forms latent cysts in brain and muscle that can reactivate when immunity is suppressed.

organisms.name: Prion (PrP^Sc)
organisms.morphology: Misfolded isoform of normal prion protein (PrP^C); no nucleic acid; resistant to proteases and standard disinfection

transmission: Iatrogenic (contaminated surgical instruments, dura mater grafts, cadaveric pituitary hormones)

labFindings: MRI: diffusion-weighted imaging ÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂ cortical ribboning, basal ganglia signal

organisms.treatment: No effective treatment ÃÂ¢ÃÂÃÂ supportive care only. Universally fatal.

The incubation period for prion diseases can be decades. Stanley Prusiner won the 1997 Nobel Prize for discovering prions.
